scope: Theorem 4.7 (A successful sampling prefix) of the manuscript “Single-exponential recovery and bounded-price strictness for metric k-median” (preprints/Single-Exponential-Recovery-and-Bounded-Price-Strictness-for-Metric-k-Median-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 125 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 823fdb284a7d3c0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 19-20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the equal-size comparison setup and Equa- tion (4.1), with 1 ≤ m ≤ M0, and use κ = 10−6. Given S and the correct guesses P, m, one run of the actual experiment has, with probability at least exp(−Cκm) for an absolute constant Cκ < ∞, a recorded prefix with the following properties: (i) Q ⊆ S0, and the balls correspond to distinct i ∈ A ⊆ B, one per such cluster, with wi ∈ Ni and ri = d(wi, i) = d(wi, O) ≤ Ri ≤ (1 + κ)ri + κr0 (wi). Consequently i ∈ Fi and P i∈A nir0(wi) ≤ 5.2P. 19 (ii) For H in Equation (4.6), B = B \ A, R∗ = S0 \ Q, and the nearest assignment sets Js, X i∈B X p∈Ni d(p, H) ≤ κP, X s∈R∗ X p∈Js d(p, H) ≤ κP. (iii) The reference retains every good proxy. The covered-client bound in Equation (4.17) holds, and for each uncovered nonempty cluster the far-client bound in Equation (4.12) holds with Ti = P p∈Ni d(p, H). The run has at most 2m + 1 recorded prefixes and takes polynomial time for fixed κ, with rational numbers of polynomial bit length. Neither its input nor its stopping decisions require O, its partition, the proxies, or S0.
